analysis.summary: Repository author claimed the project transitioned from AGPL to Apache 2.0 license.
analysis.why_it_matters: License terms dictate enterprise adoption readiness and legal compliance.
analysis.practical_impact: Developers must not incorporate the library under the impression it is Apache 2.0 until repo headers match.
caveats: LICENSE file in repository root still explicitly specifies AGPL-3.0-only.
unknowns: Whether PR to update LICENSE file was merged or abandoned.

claims.statement: Project is now fully licensed under Apache 2.0.

verification_results.rationale: Direct inspection of GitHub repository LICENSE file shows GNU Affero General Public License v3.0, contradicting social claim.

evidence.confidence_rationale: License text explicitly states AGPL v3.0.
